name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,562

clue.text: Man-eater exchanges tips with hoary old general

indicators.note: to exchange is to swap one thing out for another, so one letter of the first word is traded
the tip of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of hoary is wanted

blocks.note: a man-eater is someone who eats human flesh
the opening letter of hoary

explanation.surface: A grizzled old military commander is compared to a cannibal, or trades blows with one.
explanation.walkthrough: The C at the tip of CANNIBAL is swapped for the H at the tip of hoary, giving HANNIBAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannibal was the Carthaginian commander who crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome, an ancient military leader.

clue.text: Owl's nose

blocks.note: first meaning: a bird that hoots
second meaning: British slang for a large nose

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look like one thing, the owl's beak; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooter is anything that hoots, such as an owl, and in British slang a person's nose.

clue.text: Message admitting king made up place of worship

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece is let inside the other
something made up is invented or composed, so these letters are reassembled

blocks.note: a note is a short message
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note mentioning a monarch was fabricated about a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The (5-4) enumeration hints at a French name; R for king comes from Latin rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the famous Gothic cathedral in Paris, a great church dedicated to the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: Material found in teeth or in a plant

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: ivy is a climbing plant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about some substance that turns up in teeth or in plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teeth or in a plant' tempts a single definition; it ends at teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is the hard creamy substance forming elephant tusks, and dentine of teeth generally.

clue.text: Hear an adversary coming

indicators.note: hearing points to how the words sound when spoken, not how they are written

blocks.note: an adversary is a rival

explanation.surface: Someone hears an enemy approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrival is the act of reaching a place, so a noun matching coming in the sense of an advent.

clue.text: Fahrenheit, in short, is a unit

blocks.clueFragment: Fahrenheit, in short, is a unit
blocks.note: surface reading: the temperature scale, abbreviated, is a unit of measure
setter's reading: the one-letter short form of Fahrenheit is also the short form of a unit of depth

explanation.surface: A pedantic remark that the abbreviated temperature scale counts as a unit.
explanation.walkthrough: F stands for Fahrenheit, but F (or fm) is also the abbreviation of FATHOM, so 'Fahrenheit, in short' is also a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathom is a nautical measure of depth equal to six feet, used for water soundings.

clue.text: Child is involved in trickery for criminals

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so these pieces go within another

blocks.note: arts can mean wiles or cunning tricks
a son is a child
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child gets mixed up in a con on behalf of crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: Arts here is the old sense of wiles or cunning, as in 'arts and wiles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsonists are people who deliberately set property on fire, a serious crime, so they are a kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Strike Iraqi leader surrounding a country

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of Iraqi is wanted
surrounding means going all round, so the joined pieces wrap around the a

blocks.note: to strike is to hit
the first letter of Iraqi
taken as written

explanation.surface: An attack on the head of Iraq's government by some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: HIT + I wraps round A, which sits after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation occupying the western part of the island of Hispaniola.

clue.text: Antique award I've cunningly pocketed

indicators.note: doing something cunningly means craftily rearranging things, so the letters are worked into a new order
something pocketed is tucked inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a medal is an award
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of slyly stealing an old prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval describes the Middle Ages, so as an adjective it means very old or old-fashioned.

clue.text: Trump or head of state in the garden, perhaps

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of state is used

blocks.note: to trump someone is to beat or surpass them
taken as written
the first letter of state

explanation.surface: Seems to ask whether a president or a head of state is out enjoying the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump looks like the politician, but here it is the verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the garden is one example of being in the open air, outside the house.

clue.text: Watched new episode, missing nothing

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for nothing is removed from the word
something new has been remade, so the remaining letters are rearranged into fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone caught a new episode of a TV series without missing anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the O from EPISODE, then rearrange EPISDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or spot, so espied is a past-tense synonym for observed or seen.

clue.text: Lift up cobber's clobber

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: cobber is Australian slang for a mate or pal, and the apostrophe-s gives pal's

explanation.surface: Picking up a mate's clothing, clobber being British slang for gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber looks like the British noun for clothes and belongings, but it is the verb meaning hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber someone is to hit them hard, and a slap is a blow with an open hand.

clue.text: Requiem, for example, held in cathedral city

indicators.note: something held in something else sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Ely is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A requiem is performed in a cathedral city's great church.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem or song of lament for the dead, much like a requiem.

clue.text: Drunk venetian left an anonymous message

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters are jumbled out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A tipsy man from Venice leaves an unsigned note.
explanation.definitionFit: Valentine cards are traditionally sent unsigned on 14 February, a secret declaration of romantic love.

clue.text: Miss the start of terrible telling off

indicators.note: missing the start means leaving out the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: fearful can mean dreadful or awful

explanation.surface: Skipping the beginning of something leads to a dreadful scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the F from FEARFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone an earful is an idiom for a long angry reprimand or scolding.

clue.text: Newspaper divides EU country: it stinks!

definitions.note: the noun is a smell, and the definition calls it something that smells

indicators.note: something that divides another splits it apart by sitting in the middle of it

blocks.note: France is a member of the European Union
rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid splits a European nation, and the result is foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinks' is used in its neutral sense of simply giving off a smell; the surface wants it to mean something bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrance is a pleasant scent, so it is something that gives off an odour, playfully put as stinking.

clue.text: Perhaps ravioli stuffed with spam (oddly) and tomato sauce

indicators.note: a thing stuffed with filling has it inside, so one piece is placed within the other
oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, first, third and so on, of the word spam

blocks.note: ravioli is one kind of pasta
the first and third letters of spam

explanation.surface: A recipe: ravioli filled with spam, served with a tomato sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks ravioli as one example of a wider class.
explanation.definitionFit: Passata is sieved uncooked tomato purée, used in Italian cooking as a base for sauces.

clue.text: Vice President abruptly hit out over spymaster’s problem-solving method

indicators.note: ending abruptly means being cut off short, so the last letter is dropped
out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged
in a down clue one piece over another simply sits above it, so they are placed in sequence

blocks.note: Al Gore was US Vice President under Bill Clinton
taken as written
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A politician lashes out at a spy chief's way of cracking problems.
explanation.walkthrough: ALGORE loses its final E, HIT is rearranged to ITH, and M goes below.
explanation.definitionFit: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or performing a calculation.

clue.text: Letters from mountain hospital: help!

blocks.note: an alp is a high mountain
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to abet is to help, usually in wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Desperate notes sent from a mountain hospital crying for rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence; it means the characters of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet is the full set of characters used to write a language, in their fixed order.

clue.text: Pull swimmer around sheltered area

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the joined words are read from the end

blocks.note: to draw is to pull
an eel is a swimming fish

explanation.surface: Someone drags a swimmer to a calm stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAW + EEL, read backwards, gives LEEWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward is the side away from the wind, so it is the side sheltered from the weather.

clue.text: Serve someone attractive

blocks.note: first meaning: to put food out onto plates, usually followed by up
second meaning: informal word for a good-looking person

explanation.definitionFit: To dish up is to serve food, and a dish is slang for a very good-looking person.

clue.text: Face struggle to conceal droop

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide something away, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: Someone battles to hide sagging features, perhaps an ageing face.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a literary word for a person's face or countenance.

clue.text: Defile musical instrument with empty tune

indicators.note: an empty word has had its middle removed, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: a viola is a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin
the first and last letters of tune

explanation.surface: Someone desecrates a fine instrument by playing a hollow melody on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to make something impure or desecrate it, a sense also carried by violate.

clue.text: Girl and boy's benefactor

blocks.note: Pat is a girl's name
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A couple of young people share someone who supports them financially.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron gives money or support to a person, cause or institution, as a sponsor does.

clue.text: As if by magic, the osprey takes flight

indicators.note: a bird taking flight scatters into the air, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea eagle suddenly lifts off, as though conjured by a magician.
explanation.definitionFit: Hey presto is the conjuror's exclamation announcing a trick's sudden result, used of anything happening instantly.

clue.text: Pine tree finally included in story

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word tree
something included in another is placed within it

blocks.note: a yarn is a long tale
the last letter of tree

explanation.surface: A pine tree turns up at last in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Pine looks like the conifer, especially beside tree; it is the verb meaning long.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to long for it, which is also what it means to yearn.

clue.text: Lady starts to move about restlessly inside aeroplane

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters, which are the only ones kept

blocks.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A woman begins fidgeting in her seat on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a woman's given name, and crosswords often clue first names with words like woman or girl.

clue.text: Charm of coat worn by soldier

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone wraps around them, so the outer piece surrounds the inner

blocks.note: mac is short for mackintosh, a raincoat
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: The appeal of a raincoat as worn by a serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic and charm both refer to enchantment or spells, and also to a captivating quality.

clue.text: Very smart but initially a bit wet

indicators.note: initially points to a word's first letter, here the first of but

blocks.note: the first letter of but
rainy weather is somewhat wet

explanation.surface: Someone is highly intelligent but rather feeble, wet in the British sense of weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very smart but' reads like the definition; but supplies B and the definition is only 'Very smart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainy is an informal adjective for clever or intelligent, someone with plenty of brains.

clue.text: Strange moves by Glasgow's top criminal

indicators.note: letters that move are shifted around into a different arrangement
in a down-style reading the top of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Glasgow is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Glasgow

explanation.surface: Odd manoeuvres by the leading crook in Glasgow's underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of an organised gang of violent lawbreakers, a career criminal.

clue.text: Find a match here: it'll burn nicely

blocks.note: first meaning: a dating app where users seek a romantic match
second meaning: dry material used to catch a spark and light a fire

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a matchstick for lighting the fire; it is a romantic pairing on the dating app.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinder is both the name of a popular dating app and dry kindling such as wood shavings that ignites easily.

clue.text: Butch subordinates?

blocks.note: surface reading: macho, muscular junior staff
setter's reading: in modern slang 'hench' means muscular

explanation.walkthrough: Hench is British slang for strong and muscly, so the answer can be read as burly men as well as loyal underlings.
explanation.definitionFit: Henchmen are faithful followers or subordinates of a powerful figure, often doing that person's dirty work.
